condition: Lung mass on a chest X-ray
summary: 64-year-old smoker whose pre-operative chest X-ray shows a spiculated right upper lobe mass.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Chest X-ray shows a lung mass
inputs.hpi: Pre-operative chest X-ray before an inguinal hernia repair. On questioning: cough for two months, one episode of blood-streaked sputum, 5 kg weight loss. No fever or night sweats.

imaging.name: Chest X-ray
imaging.result: 3 cm spiculated mass in the right upper lobe. No effusion, no consolidation.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 Suspected cancer: recognition and referral — lung and pleural cancers
guideline.section: 1.1.1: suspected cancer pathway referral if chest X-ray findings suggest lung cancer or aged 40 and over with unexplained haemoptysis

rationale: Entry point: an incidental imaging finding. NG12 referral criteria are met by the X-ray alone; the loop goes back to the history (haemoptysis, weight loss, smoking) and the examination (clubbing).
